chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Soehan from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammad from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu Usamah Zayd al-Shahham said:

A man said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Do I delay the Maghrib prayer until the stars become distinct?' He said, 'He said: That is Khatthabiyyah (a reference to a specific practice/attitude). Indeed, Jibril (peace be upon him) descended upon Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) when the sun's disk set.'

key_terms.خَطَّابِيَّةٌ: Khatthabiyyah (a term indicating a specific manner or deviation, often associated with the people of Khatthab or a specific practice of delay)

ai.seo_question: When does the Maghrib prayer time begin according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies delaying Maghrib until star visibility as 'Khatthabiyyah' (a deviation from the Sunnah), anchoring the prayer's onset to the precise moment of sunset as revealed by Jibril. This highlights the Shia emphasis on strict adherence to the divine timing of prayers established during the Prophet's era, contrasting it with later jurisprudential variations regarding the definition of twilight.
